reviewer: Grok (independent read-only source review; did not author 007)
verdict: NO_CONCRETE_DEFECT. The frozen delta is the D4 kernel-message record after a signal reap. Pre-spawn control flow is unchanged. The journal lines fit the 1024-byte bound, and a one- or two-attempt session result stays under the 16384-byte exporter cap. The record is not an input to wait status, signals, completion, or has_failures. Source acceptance only. Host tests are not a Darwin run, and this review does not admit a native build or a boot.

binding.replay: verify_checkpoint.py with assertions enabled printed: Verified007 cumulative 23 and incremental 2 files, full tree and dependencies; source only. It wrote only a temp scratch directory. Exit 0.
binding.tree_delta: Independent logical-byte compare of 006/source and 007/source, skipping target/.git/__pycache__, is 3966 files each. Exactly two paths differ: crates/wm-darwin/src/applications.rs 59922339 to 6908ae34, and crates/wm-darwin/src/launch_audit.rs 559606e4 to 22283894. Those are the incremental_changed_files. The cumulative changed_files list of 23 is the history versus the keyboard-only baseline.

d4.placement: spawn_using calls the shim, then OwnedChild::new only if child_created is 1. The new kernel_messages field is set to None in that constructor, after the shim returns. poll_using calls query_kernel_messages only after WaitState::Reaped and only when WIFSIGNALED, and only once. Application::service journals that value after exit_reason and cs_at_exit and before observe. A normal exit and a still-running child do not read.
d4.pre_spawn: from-006.patch does not change launch_at before spawn_using, the spawn request, or the C shim call. begin() pushes the Attempt, which now carries Option<KernelMessages>, before the shim. That value is None, so it does not allocate the line vector. The audit vector is a Vec of Attempt. gates_ms alone is 160 bytes, so the record is far above the 256-byte malloc class of the 248-byte spawn attributes. I did not measure sizeof(Attempt) and I did not re-run cargo. The 256 KiB proc_kmsgbuf buffer is allocated only on the signal-reap path, which is after the first spawn and before any later spawn.
d4.bounds: append still refuses a line longer than 1024 bytes or a journal past 2 MiB. The largest KernelMessages journal summary I formatted with attempt 127, ms u64::MAX, and u32/u64::MAX counters is 171 bytes. The largest KernelMessage text line is 300 bytes. Both are under 1024. The snapshot adds at most 2280 bytes per signal-reaped attempt (one summary plus eight 240-byte lines). Attempt 003's session-result.txt was 1747 bytes. One or two attempts of that shape stay under the exporter cap of 16384 in desktop-records.c. The writer itself does not enforce 16384.
d4.outcome: has_failures reads the audit error, attempt failure strings, launch_failure, status error, and Incomplete completion. It does not read kernel_messages. The host test kernel_messages_are_read_once_and_only_after_a_signal_reap keeps the SIGKILL as a failure. The record is not an admission.
d4.proc_kmsgbuf: The Apple declaration matches libproc.h: int proc_kmsgbuf(void *, uint32_t). libproc.c returns 0 when __proc_info fails. proc_kernmsgbuf requires suser and otherwise returns EPERM, after an optional MAC check. log_dmesg copies the newest bytes when the caller buffer is smaller. Canonical libSystem 8ff49e0c defines _proc_kmsgbuf and _geteuid. Host builds return Unsupported and do not call it.

residuals: The larger Attempt is allocated before the first spawn. It is not in the 248-byte size class. It can still change other heap traffic. The same kind of audit-field growth in 005 and 006 did not stop the first app from dying. This review does not prove the uninitialized spawn-attribute bytes are unchanged.
The 256 KiB read runs before a second spawn when the first child was signal-reaped. It does not run before the first spawn.

A successful log_dmesg copies at least the trailing NUL, so a zero return is a failure and the stored errno is the one proc_kmsgbuf left. An empty success is not how this kernel wrapper reports a log.
The Apple proc_kmsgbuf path is compiled by the Darwin type-check only. It has not run.
